request.spec:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
When a grade has no rate in force on a date on a sheet nor on its parents, a sheet that was
cloned uses the rate of the sheet it was cloned from (and so on up that sheet's parents and
source).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A cloned sheet now falls back to the rates of the sheet it was cloned from. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests, with no deadlocks in the app log.

**The change**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V90__sheet_source.sql`, adds a `sheet_source` table that records which sheet each clone was made from. Like the parent link, it isn't part of the as-of history.
- **Clone:** `CloneService` writes that record when it makes a clone.
- **Rate lookup:** `SettingService.lineageOf` decides which sheets a rate is looked for in. It now checks the sheet and its parents (up to three levels) first. If none has a rate, it moves to the sheet it was cloned from and that sheet's parents, then that sheet's own source, and so on. Each sheet is checked only once, so a loop can't run forever.

  Everything that works out rates goes through `lineageOf`, so dues, rollups, audit lines and the `rate-current-*` values all pick up the fallback. The front end needed no change.
- **As-of view:** `SheetHistory.restoreWithParents` follows the same chain, so viewing a clone "as of" an earlier date uses the same fallback.

**Separate fix: a deadlock that was already there.** Scenario 3 doesn't clone anything, but it failed every time. I disabled my rate change and re-ran it, and it still failed, so the bug was already in the app.

The cause: after the sheet's today changes, the screen reloads people, settings, pools and crews as they stood on an earlier date. To answer each of those reads, the server rewrites the sheet's rows, including its claim-number counter, inside a transaction it then undoes. A claim being opened at the same moment deadlocked with that rewrite, and the open was refused.

I fixed this in `AsOfFilter` with a lock: changes can still run alongside each other, but a read of an earlier date now runs on its own. The downside is that while one of those reads runs, every change waits, on every sheet. Those reads are short, but it is a global lock. It's outside the change you asked for, so you may want to look at it separately.
